items: Start Your Incident Log: Open a secure personal document tonight and title it your incident log — it must be stored somewhere your employer cannot access like a personal cloud account.
Start Your Incident Log: Record every retaliatory event with exact dates, times, locations, and the names of any witnesses or participants present during each incident.
Start Your Incident Log: Write down the specific impact of each incident on your work assignments, career trajectory, or professional reputation to prove the cumulative damage.
Start Your Incident Log: Track your complaint filing date alongside the timeline of negative treatment to establish the pattern that proves your complaint came first.
Protect Your Evidence: Save all work emails, Slack messages, and calendar invites that document your assignments, performance, and communications before you lose access to them.
Protect Your Evidence: Store copies of all written performance reviews, feedback documents, and assignment confirmations in your personal email so you control the copies.
Protect Your Evidence: Keep physical or digital backup copies at home or with a trusted person outside your workplace to ensure evidence survives any device revocation.
Protect Your Evidence: Never store your incident log or evidence on company devices, company email, shared drives, or any system your employer can monitor or delete.

Make Strategic Moves: Refrain from filing additional complaints or confronting your manager right now — these reactions typically worsen your position and give them justification for more retaliation.
Make Strategic Moves: Identify three colleagues who witnessed your work quality or treatment and maintain those professional relationships as potential references for future opportunities.
Make Strategic Moves: Quietly update your resume and start exploring external opportunities without signaling distress to employers who may still be watching your activity.
Make Strategic Moves: Decide whether to stay or leave based on documented facts rather than panic — your incident log should show whether this situation has a viable path forward or requires an exit.
